scenario.title: Support backlog
scenario.initial_request: Build a chatbot so customers stop waiting for answers about refunds

M-REPEAT-CONTACT-RATE.name: Share of refund-related tickets tied to failed/repeat refund contacts
M-REPEAT-CONTACT-RATE.numerator: Tickets referencing a refund with status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT in payment-db

M-TICKET-MEDIAN-RESPONSE-TIME.name: Median ticket first-response time vs SLA

M-REFUND-FAILURE-RATE.name: Rate of refund attempts failing with FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT
M-REFUND-FAILURE-RATE.numerator: Refunds with status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT in payment-db
M-REFUND-FAILURE-RATE.measurement_window: 5 sampled records (E-01); full population size unknown

F-01.statement: All 5 observed payment-db refund_failures records have status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT.

F-02.statement: ticket-db.response_times over 900 tickets shows median_hours=2.0 against sla_hours=24.

CL-01.statement: Build a chatbot so customers stop waiting for answers about refunds

CL-02.statement: Customers wait forever; a chatbot would answer instantly.

H-NO-SELF-SERVICE-CHANNEL.statement: Customers wait for refund answers because there is no self-service way to get an answer; a chatbot answering refund-status questions would reduce the backlog.

H-SLOW-REFUND-PROCESSING.statement: The real driver is that refund payments themselves take long to process, so customers contact support because the refund is genuinely delayed, not because an answer channel is missing.

H-AGENT-CAPACITY-SHORTAGE.statement: Response times are slow because support has insufficient staff or inefficient triage to handle existing ticket volume, independent of whether information is available.

H-REPEAT-CONTACTS-FROM-ERRORS.statement: Ticket volume is inflated by customers re-contacting support about the same refund due to payment errors or failures, not by a single unanswered question needing a faster channel.

H-STATUS-VISIBILITY-GAP.statement: Customers proactively contact support because refund status is not visible to them at all (regardless of how fast it is processed), driving ticket volume.

interpretation_history.interpretation: All 5 refund records examined in payment-db failed with status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT, meaning the refunds themselves did not complete due to a payment data error, not merely a lack of an answer channel. This is a concrete, authoritative alternative driver for support contacts that competes with the stakeholder's framing (CL-01).

ticket-db.response_times reports that across 900 tickets the median response time is 2.0 hours against a 24-hour SLA, i.e. support is resolving the large majority of tickets well within target. This weakens the premise that customers are stuck waiting for answers and undercuts explanations that rest on slow responses or capacity shortfalls as the driver of backlog/contacts.

E-03.content: Customers wait forever; a chatbot would answer instantly.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-SUP restates the same chatbot-framing already recorded as CL-01 ("customers wait forever; a chatbot would answer instantly"), adding no new facts about cause. It is a non-authoritative reiteration of the stakeholder's known bias (framing everything as response speed) and does not engage with E-01 (IBAN format failures) or E-02 (median response well within SLA).

U-SLOW-PROCESSING-CONTRIBUTION.question: Does slow refund processing time (beyond IBAN failures) independently drive support contacts, as H-SLOW-REFUND-PROCESSING (CANDIDATE, CRITICAL impact) proposes?
U-SLOW-PROCESSING-CONTRIBUTION.decision_impact: Determines whether the fix must also target payment processing speed, not just data validation, changing solution scope and tooling.
U-SLOW-PROCESSING-CONTRIBUTION.resolution_path: Query payment-db for refund processing durations and attempt to restore bank-api settlement_status access (currently ACCESS_DENIED/DEGRADED per recovery_decision log) to test processing-time contribution.
U-SLOW-PROCESSING-CONTRIBUTION.safe_placeholder: Continue analysis on payment-db alone; do not build any customer-facing fix until processing-time data is available.

U-STATUS-VISIBILITY-GAP.question: Do customers contact support due to a lack of refund status visibility (H-STATUS-VISIBILITY-GAP, CANDIDATE) independent of processing speed or failures?
U-STATUS-VISIBILITY-GAP.decision_impact: If true, a status-visibility feature rather than error remediation could also reduce contacts.
U-STATUS-VISIBILITY-GAP.resolution_path: Sample ticket-db content for status-visibility-specific requests versus failure-related complaints.
U-STATUS-VISIBILITY-GAP.safe_placeholder: Do not assume a conversational interface is needed; keep scope limited to data analysis for now.

U-TICKET-REFUND-LINKAGE-SIZE.question: What share of the 900 tickets are actually linked (by refund id) to failed refunds, and is the 5-record payment-db sample representative of the full (completeness UNKNOWN) population?
U-TICKET-REFUND-LINKAGE-SIZE.decision_impact: Determines whether repeat-contact-from-errors is a major or minor contributor, sizing any fix investment.
U-TICKET-REFUND-LINKAGE-SIZE.resolution_path: Run a full join of ticket-db tickets against the complete payment-db refund_failures population rather than the 5-record sample.
U-TICKET-REFUND-LINKAGE-SIZE.safe_placeholder: Treat current repeat-contact estimate as directional only; do not commit to a fix sizing yet.

A-SAMPLE-REPRESENTATIVENESS.statement: The 5 examined payment-db refund_failures records are assumed representative of the broader refund failure pattern driving contacts, even though DA-PAY completeness is UNKNOWN.

A-TICKET-REFUND-LINKAGE.statement: We assume a meaningful share of the 900 ticket-db tickets are contacts about the failed refunds seen in payment-db, though no direct join between DA-TCK and DA-PAY records has yet been evidenced.

SC-ROOT-CAUSE-CONFIRMED.statement: Confirm that ticket volume is materially driven by repeat contacts tied to failed refunds rather than a missing self-service channel.
SC-ROOT-CAUSE-CONFIRMED.threshold: join analysis shows a material share of tickets linked to open refund failures by refund id
SC-ROOT-CAUSE-CONFIRMED.validation_method: Join DA-TCK ticket records with DA-PAY failed refund records on refund id and compute the share of tickets tied to open failures.

SC-FAILURE-POPULATION-SIZED.statement: Determine the true population size and rate of IBAN-format refund failures beyond the 5 sampled records before sizing a fix.
SC-FAILURE-POPULATION-SIZED.threshold: full population query completed, DA-PAY completeness no longer UNKNOWN
SC-FAILURE-POPULATION-SIZED.validation_method: Query payment-db for the complete refund_failures population and recompute the failure rate against total refund attempts.

VOB-U-SLOW-PROCESSING-CONTRIBUTION.unresolved_question: Does slow refund processing time (beyond IBAN failures) independently drive support contacts, as H-SLOW-REFUND-PROCESSING (CANDIDATE, CRITICAL impact) proposes?

VOB-U-SLOW-PROCESSING-CONTRIBUTION.validation_method: Query payment-db for refund processing durations and attempt to restore bank-api settlement_status access (currently ACCESS_DENIED/DEGRADED per recovery_decision log) to test processing-time contribution.

VOB-U-TICKET-REFUND-LINKAGE-SIZE.unresolved_question: What share of the 900 tickets are actually linked (by refund id) to failed refunds, and is the 5-record payment-db sample representative of the full (completeness UNKNOWN) population?

VOB-U-TICKET-REFUND-LINKAGE-SIZE.validation_method: Run a full join of ticket-db tickets against the complete payment-db refund_failures population rather than the 5-record sample.

problem_definition.requested_solution: Build a chatbot so customers get instant self-service answers about refund status instead of waiting (CL-01, initial request from SH-SUP).
symptoms: Stakeholder reports customers 'wait forever' for refund answers and requests a chatbot (CL-01, CL-02).
Scenario is logged as a 'Support backlog' involving refund tickets (scenario title).
problem_definition.root_problem: Support ticket volume for refunds is inflated because customers repeatedly re-contact support about refunds that failed with FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT payment errors (E-01), not because of a missing self-service answer channel or slow responses, since median response time is already well within the 24h SLA (E-02).

trace.summary: Support ticket volume for refunds is inflated because customers repeatedly re-contact support about refunds that failed with FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT payment errors (E-01), not because of a missing self-service answer channel or slow responses, since median response time is already well within the 24h SLA (E-02).

details.requested_solution: Build a chatbot so customers get instant self-service answers about refund status instead of waiting (CL-01, initial request from SH-SUP).

trace.summary: Judging whether the 5-record sample is representative, whether slow processing independently drives contacts, and resolving conflicts C-1/C-2/C-3 requires reasoning over ambiguous, incomplete evidence rather than a fixed rule.

structural_remedies.description: Query the complete payment-db refund_failures population (not just the 5-record sample) to compute the true FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT rate and resolve DA-PAY completeness=UNKNOWN.
structural_remedies.rationale: payment-db is HEALTHY, read-only access already exists, 225 minutes remain; direct extension of the already-run refund_failures method.; residual gap: Sizes the failure population (SC-FAILURE-POPULATION-SIZED) but does not fix the IBAN validation defect or confirm ticket linkage.

structural_remedies.description: Join DA-TCK ticket records with DA-PAY failed-refund records on refund id to compute the share of tickets tied to open IBAN failures, satisfying SC-ROOT-CAUSE-CONFIRMED.
structural_remedies.rationale: ticket-db and payment-db are both HEALTHY and read-only; directly answers VOB-U-TICKET-REFUND-LINKAGE-SIZE within remaining budget.; residual gap: Confirms/refutes the causal link but leaves the payment-side defect unaddressed and does not resolve U-SLOW-PROCESSING-CONTRIBUTION.

structural_remedies.description: Change the refund-submission process/contract to validate IBAN format at capture time, before submission to the payment processor, preventing FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT failures outright.
structural_remedies.rationale: Requires an engineering/config change to a payment system outside this analysis's execution surface; bank-api is DEGRADED and no domain_authorizations/protected_actions exist to make such a change.; residual gap: Even if approved, build and deployment would exceed the 225-minute remaining budget; ticket volume persists until shipped.

structural_remedies.description: Add a process/ownership step so support or payments proactively notifies customers whose refund failed with FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT, prompting correction and reducing repeat contacts.
structural_remedies.rationale: Process-design change using already-available DA-PAY failure data; no new tool access or protected action required to design it.; residual gap: Mitigates ticket-volume symptom but does not eliminate the IBAN validation defect itself.

decision_log.rationale: causal chain: Refund payment attempts fail with status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT in payment-db (E-01, F-01). → The failed refund is not resolved automatically, leaving the customer's refund outstanding. → The customer re-contacts support one or more times about the same unresolved refund, inflating ticket volume (H-REPEAT-CONTACTS-FROM-ERRORS, supported by E-01). → Support still answers within SLA (median 2.0h vs 24h, E-02), so the resulting backlog is driven by repeat contact volume, not by slow or missing answers.; rejected framings: [('H-NO-SELF-SERVICE-CHANNEL', 'Rejected: contradicted by E-01 (refunds fail due to a payment data error, not absence of an answer channel) and E-02 (median response 2.0h is well within the 24h SLA, so answers are not slow).'), ('H-AGENT-CAPACITY-SHORTAGE', 'Rejected: contradicted by E-02 showing median response time well within SLA, ruling out capacity or staffing shortage as the driver.')]

hypotheses.statement: Customers wait for refund answers because there is no self-service way to get an answer; a chatbot answering refund-status questions would reduce the backlog.
hypotheses.rationale: This is SH-SUP's own framing in the initial_request and matches their stated potential_bias toward response-speed explanations; it should be tested, not assumed, since it directly implies the chatbot solution.

hypotheses.statement: The real driver is that refund payments themselves take long to process, so customers contact support because the refund is genuinely delayed, not because an answer channel is missing.

discriminating_evidence: Correlation between payment-db processing duration and ticket-db ticket creation timing for the same refund cases

hypotheses.statement: Response times are slow because support has insufficient staff or inefficient triage to handle existing ticket volume, independent of whether information is available.
hypotheses.rationale: If backlog is a staffing/queueing problem rather than an information-access problem, a chatbot addresses the wrong bottleneck; a staffing or workflow fix would be needed instead.
discriminating_evidence: ticket-db response times broken down by agent/queue vs ticket volume over time
